standard.title: Reflect on influences on visual arts practice
standard.description: reflect on the way they and other visual artists respond to influences to inspire, develop and resolve choices they make in their own visual arts practice
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have begun identifying an emerging personal style and have investigated artists from diverse contexts. They can make informed choices based on documented experimentation. They have not yet systematically reflected on how personal, cultural and contextual influences shape their own practice, or used investigation of others' influences to understand their own.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students reflect on the ways they and other visual artists respond to influences — using this understanding to inspire, develop and resolve choices in their own visual arts practice.

nodes.label: Identifying personal influences
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can investigate and reflect on the role of their own culture, family and personal experiences as influences on their visual arts practice.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one personal influence (cultural background, family, personal experience) and explain how it has shaped one aspect of their practice.
nodes.typical_width: Investigate how culture, family and personal experiences influence what they are drawn to, what they make and how they make it; document reflections in journal form; connect personal influences to specific choices visible in their work.
wider: Explore current issues of personal importance (local or global) as a starting point for artwork — document how the issue connects to your own experiences and values, and how this shapes your visual response
Investigate how your visual arts practice can explore and represent personal experiences — research how other artists have approached self-awareness and emotional awareness; develop your own approach
nodes.hinge_reason: Personal influence reflection is the foundation for this descriptor — students who cannot identify their own influences cannot meaningfully compare them with other artists' influences, and cannot use influence understanding to resolve making choices.

response_modes.reason: Influence reflection is not automatic — students need structured prompts ('What experiences have shaped what I make? What would be absent from my work without my background?') to surface influences that are invisible precisely because they are familiar.

success_criteria: Identifies at least one personal influence (cultural, familial or experiential)
Explains how it has shaped at least one aspect of their practice — a choice, direction or recurring concern

nodes.label: Investigating other artists' influences
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can investigate how other artists respond to their own influences — examining accounts of their practices to understand the many factors that can shape a visual arts practice.
nodes.minimum_width: Investigate one artist's accounts of their influences and explain how at least one influence is visible in their work.
nodes.typical_width: Investigate a diverse range of visual artists — including artists from different countries and contexts (e.g. the Asia region) — through accounts of the influences on their work; analyse how influences shape specific artistic choices; connect this understanding to your own practice.
wider: Investigate First Nations Australian artists and their reflections on how personal and community experiences shape their visual arts practice — reflect on what these accounts suggest about how you might represent your own experiences
Analyse how artists structure artworks to represent ideas — use Viewpoints questions to unpack the relationship between the artist's influences and their compositional and material choices

response_modes.reason: Students who investigate only one type of artist (e.g. Western contemporary) develop a narrow model of what influences can be. A diverse range — including cross-cultural and First Nations — expands their understanding of the range of factors that can shape making.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: First Nations Australian artists' accounts of their influences are distinctively rich — they foreground Country/Place, community and responsibility as influences alongside personal experience, offering a genuinely different model of how influences shape practice.
success_criteria: Investigates at least one artist's accounts of their influences
Explains how at least one influence is visible in specific choices in the work

nodes.label: Using influence understanding to resolve choices
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use their understanding of personal and external influences to inspire, develop and resolve choices in their own visual arts practice.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one making choice that was directly inspired or resolved by understanding a personal or external influence.
nodes.typical_width: Reflect on, evaluate and resolve choices in artworks as they progress — through informal discussion, journal reflection or multimedia evaluation; connect choices to identified influences; use understanding of how other artists respond to influences to inform own resolutions.
wider: Explore a current global or local issue as a starting point — research how artists have used their influences to address similar issues; reflect on how your own background shapes your response and use this to resolve a making choice
Compare your own influence reflections with those of artists you have investigated — identify parallels and differences and explain what this reveals about your own practice

response_modes.reason: Personal influence reflection and external artist investigation come together in the resolution of a specific making choice. The integration is evidenced when the student can trace a decision back to an understood influence — their own or inspired by another artist's approach.

success_criteria: Identifies at least one making choice that was inspired or resolved by understanding a personal or external influence
Explains the connection — not just 'I was influenced by X' but how the influence shaped the specific choice
